messages:
Alex R: FYI — customer ACME reported multiple streaming requests being marked as 5xx. They say client disconnected but we're billing them for failed requests. Ticket: https://acme.atlassian.net/browse/ACME-3219 
Alex R: Payloads are moderate (~3-6s token stream). They see: 
```
write error: broken pipe
proxy: downstream closed connection during write
request_id=trc_01E123ABC
```
Alex R: They included curl they used for repro (node env):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \ 
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \ 
  -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams
```
Maria G: Thanks — can you paste the full trace/ingest link + sample request id? Also which plan/customer (hosted/dedicated)?
Alex R: Trace link: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/trc_01E123ABC
Customer is hosted (paid, low volume). Attached are logs around the event: 
```
2026-02-18T14:02:11.123Z gateway info request_id=trc_01E123ABC started
2026-02-18T14:02:14.987Z runtime info forwarded chunked payload to model
2026-02-18T14:02:18.004Z gateway warn write to client failed: write tcp 10.0.0.5:443->203.0.113.45:54321: write: broken pipe
2026-02-18T14:02:18.005Z gateway error marking 5xx request_id=trc_01E123ABC reason="client disconnected during write"
```
Jamal S: Repro attempt notes: I ran a local proxy that closes connection with FIN mid-stream. I see identical write errors on the gateway. Kernel-level errno shows EPIPE. Important: client FIN happens *after* we wrote last chunk; TCP FIN vs RST timing differs by client.
Jamal S: Quick python repro (simulates client half-close):
```
import socket, time
s = socket.socket()
s.connect(("api.redwood.ai", 443))
# upgraded to TLS etc omitted here for brevity
# send request headers + initial chunk
# then close socket abruptly from client side to simulate FIN
s.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)
# server writes -> gets EPIPE / broken pipe
```
Theo C: TL;DR — this looks like a client-initiated half-close (FIN) that lands while gateway is writing chunks. Our current billing/classification logic treats any write failure as gateway 5xx. We need a discriminator so client-aborts != internal 5xx for billing.
Maria G: Do we have metric labels for socket errno? If we can tag EPIPE/ECONNRESET as downstream-abort and exclude from 5xx billing, that would resolve customer's immediate billing dispute.
Jamal S: Right now we log text but don't export errno to the request metric. I can add an enum label socket_error_type with values {none, epipe, econnreset, other} and increment counters. Then change billing rule: if socket_error_type in (epipe, econnreset) AND upstream wrote >0 bytes, classify as client_abort not gateway_5xx.
Alex R: Customer asked for temporary credit while we investigate. Support recommended 100% credit for 4 requests flagged incorrectly (they provided timestamps). Canops? :eyes:
Maria G: I'll approve provisional credit and file refund. Submit the amounts and request ids and I will sign off.
Theo C: Tech plan: jamal will open PR to: (1) export socket_error_type as metric + add logging with numeric errno, (2) adjust billing classification to prefer client_abort when downstream socket errno exists and write offset > 0, (3) add integration test simulating FIN during chunk write. Target: canary deploy tomorrow to prod api-gateway canary pool.
Jamal S: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/7123 — includes unit tests and a small metric change. Note: need ops to add metric cardinality whitelist for socket_error_type.
SRE-Bot: scheduled deploy to canary cluster: gateway:v5.8.2-pr7123 at 2026-02-19T02:00:00Z (canary 2 nodes). Monitor: error_rate_stream_write, socket_error_type:e.pipe, billing_client_abort_count.
Alex R: I added note in the ticket and told the customer we've started a canary deploy and will credit affected calls. They said thanks and asked if we can provide the stack logs for transparency.
Theo C: Next steps: Jamal — follow up after canary with metrics. Maria — issue provisional credit and close with the customer. Alex — paste final logs to ticket and copy to customer. I'll follow up to discuss changing our 5xx heuristics more broadly (possible false-negatives).
SRE-Bot: canary passed basic health checks after 30m. Observed a drop in gateway error->5xx tagging where socket_error_type==epipe. Will promote if no regressions in 2h. :white_check_mark:
Customer-Support: Customer acknowledged credit and closing for now. May reopen if they see new incidents. :+1:
